$comment: Un-canonicalizable request (URL-CANONICALIZATION.md §3.3.5). A's declared prefix is /v1/cluster; A's verifier observes a path /v2/cluster/mcp that does NOT start with the prefix and is not equal to the prefix. The verifier MUST reject with bad_request_sig BEFORE attempting any signature verification.
name: uncanonicalizable-reject
scenario: Misrouted request / stale prefix declaration / cross-deployment leakage
$comment_p_canonical: P would have computed canonical bytes over path-suffix /mcp (its declared prefix at signing time was /v1/cluster). For reference, the P-side canonical-bytes SHA-256 matches prefix-strip.json: 7a3ed325013918d6f02f6fe7eecef8320947f31836b5e7dfd68a3b3fd408314e. But A NEVER reaches signature verification; rejection happens at §3.3.3 prefix-strip when /v2/cluster/mcp does not start with /v1/cluster + '/'.
verifier_rejection_detail: request path does not start with declared prefix; un-canonicalizable per §3.3.5
$comment_receipts: RECEIPTS.md §5 inherits this: A MUST NOT emit a receipt over the un-canonicalizable request. The receipt would commit to bytes P cannot reproduce, so P would reject it; the rejection happens at the lease layer instead.
